answer: Radio multilateration suppresses Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to physical broadcast coordinates. Receivers on an oceanic island, a mountain ridge, and a polar glacier timestamp incoming pulses to resolve emitter locations. An attacker must operate discrete radio transmitters across separate zones, incurring heavy hardware and leasing costs per persona. However, atmospheric refraction and multipath reflections can skew pulse timings, mistakenly rejecting legitimate agents.
